analysis.title: Gold Futures: 5 Straight Weeks of Speculative Selling
key_insights: Per CFTC Commitment of Traders, speculative gold selling accelerated over Oct 20-27. Managed Money, Other and Non-Reportable sold $8bn, the 5th straight week of bearish flows, for a cumulative $19.5bn since Sept 22. Liquidation ($5.2bn) and new shorts ($2.8bn) both contributed.
Other and Non-Reportable accounted for ~95% of the total selling. Other gross long selling ($4bn) was the largest component.

This helps explain muted gold price action despite lower real rates. Gold fell 1.6% over the window while US 10-year real yields dropped 11bp. Brent rose 4.1% and the Dollar rose 0.6% in the same period.

GS suggests fear of sovereign liquidity management and Dollar resilience may have triggered some of the Other unwinds. Rolling 6-month correlations of Other gross longs with DXY and with the 1st Brent contract were moderately negative.

Other gross longs on Oct 27 were still above their 2-year median in notional terms and as a percentage of open interest, so GS calls the set-up still challenging. Managed Money net positioning stayed relatively low.
Gold's weakness extended into month-end. From Oct 27-30 gold lost 4.3% as Brent rose another 3.7%, which overshadowed retracements in DXY and real yields.
Gold options showed hedging and/or outright downside implementation. 3-month implied volatility and normalized 25-delta put-call skew both richened, with skew reaching an 85% 1-year rank.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Real yields moderated, which would normally support gold, but gold fell 1.6% over the same window.
Higher Brent coincided with gold weakness and appeared to overshadow retracements in DXY and real yields.
Dollar resilience potentially contributed to Other unwinds in gold.

risk_factors: Elevated Other gross long positioning leaves room for further unwinds in gold.
Brent strength and Dollar resilience can weigh on gold even as real yields fall.
Fear of sovereign liquidity management could trigger further Other unwinds.
